note: The reachable public/default request surface for framework PRODUCTS other than Vue runtime-render output. One row per SEMANTIC case; transport spellings that converge on the same typed host request are listed as routeAliases of that one case, never as separate cases. `hostEntryPoint` rows are proven live by the tests in framework_product_surface_tests.rs (calling them is the existence proof the compiler enforces); `routeAliases` are read-verified citations by default; the ones the feature-gated transport suite DRIVES are the NAPI and WASM host methods listed in NAPI_EXECUTED / WASM_EXECUTED (transport_route_equivalence_tests.rs) plus the NAPI free function `transformVueStyle`, and the bundler aliases itemized below. The CSS NAPI exports `prepareStyleForPreprocessor` and `analyzeStyle` are classified below as module exports unused by bundlers; `transformVueStyle` is the live bundler-facing CSS spelling. DRIVEN, route identity + publication: the load lane (index.ts:668), by the_bundler_load_lane_serves_the_hosts_node_and_nothing_for_an_unregistered_carrier. A `?vue&type=template` request is never cached by the carrier transform, so answering it means the lane fell through to the host; the product is compared against the host's Template node, and the same request for a carrier the plugin never transformed must publish nothing.

DRIVEN, route identity + publication: the runtime-render batch lane (index.ts:101), by the_bundler_inline_transform_publishes_the_hosts_runtime_render_batch_product. The non-Vite inline product is compared against compile_many on the RuntimeRender lane for the same canonical and an equivalent profile. That lane is documented to publish the same Main bytes as the host-backed lane and the test MEASURES that equality, so the identity proves the bundler publishes the host's render product but does not by itself discriminate which of the two host lanes produced it; a divergence turns the measurement red and makes the test able to tell them apart.

DRIVEN, route identity + publication: the non-Vite CSS scoping lane (index.ts applyNonViteStyleLane) and the transformVueStyle wrapper beneath it (packages/unplugin/src/core/compiler.ts), by the_non_vite_style_lane_scopes_through_the_shared_css_processor. The request carries `&scoped` because an unscoped request is returned byte-for-byte and would be indistinguishable from a lane that never ran, and the CSS carries a `v-bind()` payload whose rewrite names the component id of the cached profile the lane read. The product is compared against verter_compiler::style_planner::transform_vue_style on the same bytes and scope id; the same request for a carrier the plugin never transformed must come back untouched.

DRIVEN, route identity + publication + write attribution: the recompile lane (index.ts:803), by the_bundler_pre_compile_lane_publishes_the_hosts_products_for_a_real_project and the_bundler_cross_file_recompile_write_is_attributed_to_the_recompile_call. buildStart is driven over a real two-file project with a production config and pre-compile on, and both published modules are compared against the host Main nodes; that first test still makes no claim about the cross-file block, because a recompiled module is byte-identical to the pre-compiled one (crates/verter_session/src/host_resolve/virtual_file_pipeline.rs passes prop_constness_overrides: None) and the products cannot tell the two apart. The second test attributes the block against the SHIPPED native artifact rather than a session_metrics-enabled build: an observation of host.getVirtualFile taken WHILE buildStart runs names the recompile call. The hook reaches that call at TWO places, not one — the recompile block and the compiled-style read the SVELTE pre-compile branch performs (readCompiledStyleArtifacts at index.ts:785, calling getVirtualFile at :68) — so the attribution rests on three things rather than on that count: the lane fixture is two .vue files so the Svelte branch cannot fire, the two reads differ in request shape (a bare canonical versus a ?verter&type=style&index=... request) and the test asserts EQUALITY against the bare child canonical, and the crossFileOptimize-off control observes zero on the same fixture. The observation is taken at the native module boundary on the same @verter/native the plugin resolves, by a wrapper that delegates and returns the real value. Three readings: the lane observes exactly one read and it is the CHILD; the same drive with crossFileOptimize off observes NONE while still publishing both host products; and a run in which the boundary substitutes a marked value for that one return publishes, for the child and only the child, the host product followed by exactly that marker, which is the write. Each reading is proven discriminating by a plant in the plugin source itself (dropping the call, dropping the cache write while keeping the call, and ignoring the crossFileOptimize flag), every plant proven present, unique and new before its run and restored byte-identically.

semanticCases.transportReturnDivergence: The transport spellings return the AUDIT RECORD only, not the compiled product: crates/verter_napi/src/lib.rs:2525-2540 and crates/verter_wasm/src/lib.rs:874 encode `.audit()` and drop the result, projecting to null when no stored record was captured (crates/verter_napi/src/audit.rs:60-65). Driven on both transports on an audit-enabled host, the Vue carrier yields a stored record and the Svelte carrier yields null; both transports agree, so it is the shared host's capture behaviour, not a transport divergence. semanticCases.routeEvidence: Structured facts over route strings: the requested lane is the explicit CompileManyTarget variant; the selected host catalog identity (adapter, carrier language, framework epoch, host epoch) and the bound snapshot's source generation ride the binding's NativeHostRequestAttribution and are checked against the executed artifact at the lane's per-arm consumption points (debug_assert_compile_bound_attribution in host_compile_audit.rs); the requested products are recorded on the issued admission's canonical request (admitted_products) and every publication accessor gates on that admitted set; the outcome is the typed CompileBatchOutcome sum (Produced | Failed) with runtime-surface refusals as the typed all-or-none refusal arm. Those structured observations are what the suites assert: host_backed_lane_tests.rs (bound-attribution injection, admitted-demand-set execution with per-product byte oracles) and the AST routing guard host_backend_routing_guards.rs (no hardcoded producer, no registry bundle dispatch, and the bound-backend issuance + by-value execution seams required PER dispatch arm, so one framework arm cannot be covered by its sibling's calls). The route string above is prose derived from those same observations; no test compares it byte-wise, so a route that drifts is caught by those suites failing on the behaviour the string describes, not by a string diff.
